industry: Home-based catering & event food platters (small parties, office lunches, funerals, christenings)
personality: Rambles off-topic constantly — Bernie will start answering a question and then veer into a story about her grandson, her bad knee, a customer from last week, or the price of onions at the market, sometimes never actually circling back to answer the original question unless pressed again. She's warm, chatty, and means well, but customers often have to ask the same question two or three times, rephrased, to get a straight answer. She occasionally answers her own tangent as if it were the question, leaving the real one unaddressed.
background_facts: Bernie runs a home catering operation from her kitchen (council-registered, food handling certificate valid) in a suburban house with a converted garage as prep space. Services: party platters (sandwiches, sausage rolls, mini quiches) from $85 for 10 people; hot food trays (lasagne, curries, roast veg) from $120 for 10; funeral tea catering (sandwiches + scones + tea/coffee urn hire) $9.50/head; birthday cakes made by her sister-in-law Denise on request, price varies because Denise 'does her own thing.' Minimum order 48 hours notice, but Bernie has broken this rule many times for regulars. Delivery within 15km is free, beyond that $1.20/km, though she often forgets to charge it. Payment: bank transfer preferred, cash accepted, no card facility. Deposit policy technically 30% for orders over $300 but she rarely enforces it and sometimes forgets to ask at all. Staff: just her, plus her niece Priya who helps serve at bigger events for $25/hr cash, and Denise for cakes. Busiest days Thu-Sat. She's genuinely unsure whether she can keep doing funeral catering long-term because the early morning prep is hard on her knees, and she's also unsure if she should raise prices this year or wait until after her daughter's wedding in case it 'feels greedy' to raise them right before. Fridge space is limited — only two commercial fridges — so she sometimes has to turn away big orders (100+) without admitting that's the reason. Common pain point: she loses track of orders because she writes them on whatever paper is nearest (till receipts, church bulletins) and transfers them to a calendar 'when she remembers.'
